title: Sabertooth
supports: Manufacturer-described operating modes, subsea residency, docking for charging and data exchange.
limitation: Vendor claims; not an independent endurance or arbitrary repair validation. Numerical performance and six-month maintenance claim are deliberately not adopted.

title: How does pressure change with ocean depth?
supports: Approximate pressure increase of one atmosphere per ten meters depth.
limitation: Public educational explanation, not pressure-vessel design guidance. Chapter calculation uses explicitly illustrative density, depth and window area.

title: The Arrays
supports: Regional Cabled Array off Oregon supplies power, bandwidth and communications to seafloor instrumentation and profiler moorings.
limitation: Evidence of observatory infrastructure, not an autonomous subsea factory.

title: Acoustic Communications Group
supports: Acoustic communications and navigation systems support undersea telemetry, control and positioning; modem research.
limitation: Laboratory overview; no universal acoustic-link bandwidth, range or latency is claimed.

title: In-space Servicing, Assembly, and Manufacturing (ISAM)
supports: ISAM terminology and 2026 survey scope across past, present and near-future capabilities.
limitation: Survey entries span maturity levels; chapter deliberately avoids treating entry counts as operational factories. Full 2026 State of Play report was not exhaustively reviewed.

title: Mobile Servicing System
supports: Canadarm2 assembly role, Dextre maintenance, Mobile Base System and ground robotics controllers.
limitation: Historical and architectural evidence for prepared ISS tasks, not a claim of generalized autonomous servicing.

title: About Dextre
supports: Selected replaceable exterior equipment; cameras, tools, connector and controlled manipulation.
limitation: Page includes an older future-tense vision-system statement; that statement is not used to infer deployment status.

title: Robot Team Builds High-Performance Digital Structure for NASA
supports: ARMADAS ground demonstration of specialized robots assembling modular structural building blocks.
limitation: Future lunar illustrations are concept art. No orbital/lunar deployment or numerical reliability claim is inferred.

title: ESA 3D prints first metal part on the International Space Station
supports: First completed metal shape in August 2024 using ISS technology demonstrator; samples intended for Earth analysis.
limitation: Process demonstration, not certification of arbitrary replacement parts.

title: 3D-printed metal: unlocking crew autonomy
supports: Fifth sample and comparison of returned samples with ground references; publication of analysis described as forthcoming at that date.
limitation: Read together with the later October update S26. The promised complete analysis publication was not independently located.

title: Update on Status of NASA's OSAM-1 Project
supports: Initial discontinuation announcement citing technical, cost, schedule and partnership-context difficulties.
limitation: Historical decision; current narrative also checks later reassessment in S12.

title: On-orbit Servicing, Assembly, and Manufacturing 1 (OSAM-1): Headquarters announcement
supports: Reassessment of descoped launch plan, reconfirmed cancellation and orderly shutdown following congressional notification.
limitation: Page retains a conflicting generic 'Active Mission' template label; substantive cancellation announcement is used. No claim about final disposition of every hardware item.

title: Blue Alchemist Hits Major Milestone Toward Permanent and Sustainable Lunar Infrastructure
supports: Reported critical design review completion and planned 2026 autonomous simulated-lunar-environment demonstration; intended regolith-to-materials/oxygen/solar-power pathway.
limitation: Targeted follow-up searches did not establish a later completed autonomous demonstration. No lunar operation or projected economic benefit is treated as measured fact.

title: NASA Technology Helps Guard Against Lunar Dust
supports: Sharp, abrasive lunar dust and concerns involving seals, gaskets and exposed systems.
limitation: Used for environmental motivation, not to claim universal dust-removal effectiveness or completion of a flight demonstration.

title: Lunar Dust Mitigation: A Guide and Reference: First Edition (2021)
organization: NASA Technical Reports Server; Abel and colleagues
supports: Abstract frames avoidance/removal/tolerance as system trades and identifies optical, thermal, bearing and seal concerns.
limitation: 25 MB PDF exceeded retrieval limit. Detailed report guidance is not claimed as reviewed; use is restricted to accessible abstract and metadata.

title: Moon Facts
supports: Extremely tenuous lunar atmosphere and environmental context.
limitation: Global facts do not establish illumination or thermal conditions at a particular landing site.

title: Lunar Surface Technology
supports: Separate development areas for power, resource extraction, construction and dust mitigation.
limitation: Program descriptions and planned capabilities are not evidence of a complete operational lunar industry.

title: NASA's Oxygen-Generating Experiment MOXIE Completes Mars Mission
supports: 122 grams total oxygen over sixteen runs; best reported rate 12 grams/hour at 98% purity or better; atmospheric carbon-dioxide conversion.
limitation: Experimental result is not continuous production, storage, distribution or an integrated industrial-utility demonstration.

title: Mars Facts
supports: Mars orbital period about 687 Earth days; environmental context.
limitation: The chapter's approximate synodic-period arithmetic is an original simplified derivation, not a mission trajectory or launch schedule.

title: Space Communications: 7 Things You Need to Know
supports: Illustrative one-way Earth-Mars communication latency of roughly four to twenty-four minutes depending on geometry.
limitation: Range is public explanatory scale; actual delay depends on trajectory and time. Other NASA documents may round extrema differently.

title: Geometry of Mars Solar Conjunction
supports: Sun interference during conjunction and command restrictions for Mars missions; roughly twenty-six-month geometry recurrence.
limitation: No specific 2026 command-moratorium dates or universal communications outage duration are claimed.

title: Visualizing the Flow Physics of Human-Scale Mars Entry
supports: Research into retropropulsion flow physics for large Mars payloads and the difficulty of scaling entry/descent/landing.
limitation: Simulation research, not a demonstrated human-scale cargo landing.

title: Fission Surface Power
supports: Development effort for a 40-kilowatt-class lunar fission system and future-operation objective.
limitation: Program plan, not an operating lunar utility. MERIDIAN-L does not include a reactor. Chapter avoids treating target schedule as assured.

title: Advanced automation for space missions: Technical summary (NASA-CR-163827)
organization: NASA/ASEE Summer Study; NASA Technical Reports Server
supports: Historical self-replicating lunar-factory concepts; distinct material processing, parts production, construction and product output; discussion of supplied parts and closure.
limitation: 113-page technical summary inspected selectively in replication sections, not a modern feasibility validation. Historical projected costs, growth rates and timelines are not adopted.

title: In-Space Telescope Assembly: When is it worth it?
supports: iSAT study's comparison of in-space assembly with Earth-built, single-launch deployable observatories.
limitation: Concept trade study, not a flight demonstration or universal economic conclusion.

title: Tiny thrusters 3D-printed in space
supports: Fifth sample returned to Earth; earlier findings informed printing procedure; small DLR-designed thruster-shaped components intended for subsequent functional testing.
limitation: Functional testing described as next steps; no completed hot-fire performance, certification or operational use is inferred.

title: Weather on the Moon
organization: NASA Science / Goddard Space Flight Center
supports: Large differences between sunlit and shadowed lunar surface temperatures and weak exosphere.
limitation: Global environmental examples do not establish a site-specific equipment thermal budget.
